sources.title: Official DeepSeek-OCR release history
sources.evidence: The release section announces DeepSeek-OCR2 on 2026-01-27, earlier than the January 28 arXiv paper.

sources.title: DeepSeek-OCR 2: Visual Causal Flow
sources.evidence: The exact-model technical report identifies DeepSeek-AI authors, describes DeepEncoder V2 and the MoE decoder, and labels the retained decoder nominally 3B with about 500M active parameters. This is a decoder component disclosure, not a complete multimodal active count. Reopened October 27: section 3.3 explicitly retains the prior 3B MoE decoder with about 500M active parameters, and section 4.2.2 names DeepSeek-3B-A500M as the final language decoder. This directly supports a nominal 0.5B active field scoped to language_decoder.

sources.title: Official DeepSeek-OCR-2 model card
sources.evidence: The original model card publishes weights and text-prompt/image inference examples for free OCR and grounded document-to-Markdown conversion. It lists the per-image visual-token budget as 256 plus up to six 144-token crops. Fresh October 27 card read still links the exact OCR2 report and checkpoint; it introduces no conflicting complete-model active count.

sources.title: Official checkpoint configuration
sources.evidence: Configuration sets max_position_embeddings=8192, 12 language layers, first_k_dense_replace=1, 64 routed experts, 2 shared experts, and 6 routed experts per token. It uses a SAM/Qwen2 vision stack and an 896-to-1280 linear projector; use_mla=false. Fresh current configuration on October 27 retains the same 12-layer decoder and 64/6 routed, 2 shared-expert configuration.

sources.title: Official weight repository Apache 2.0 license
sources.evidence: The actual LICENSE.txt distributed with the original weights is Apache License, Version 2.0; this agrees with model-card metadata.

sources.title: Official checkpoint safetensors header
sources.evidence: Two bounded HTTP 206 byte-range requests (0-7 and 8-335159) retrieve the 335152-byte JSON header, not weight payloads. Its 2707 BF16 tensors contain 3389119360 learned elements. Exact key coverage matches the official index; code inspection identifies learned positions, queries and separator and no stored buffers or quantization scales.

sources.title: Official DeepEncoder V2 implementation
sources.evidence: The SAM positional tensors are explicit learned Parameters. Qwen2-0.5B is instantiated with 24 layers, then its token-embedding table is deleted; learned 144- and 256-query embeddings are added. Thus the released causal encoder has 358256512 parameters, rather than retaining all nominal Qwen2-0.5B parameters.

sources.title: Official OCR2 multimodal implementation
sources.evidence: The released model combines SAM, Qwen2 vision encoder, linear projector and learned view separator with the language decoder. Vision runs on prefill; the inference interface accepts images and text and emits generated text. No dedicated thinking control or tool-schema interface is documented here. Fresh October 27 implementation read confirms image encoding is guarded by input_ids.shape[1] != 1 (or training), with nonzero image input, before the autoregressive language path. The nominal decoder active count is not a full image-prefill count.

sources.title: Official OCR2 language decoder implementation
sources.evidence: The decoder implementation has learned MoE gates/experts and untied text embedding/output-head modules. Rotary caches and inverse frequencies are registered as nonpersistent buffers and are absent from the checkpoint header.

sources.title: Official OCR2 tokenizer configuration
sources.evidence: The tokenizer has no chat_template and inherits tool-call special tokens. Token presence alone does not establish trained or supported native function calling; the supplied model card and OCR inference instructions do not document such support.

sources.title: Official repository metadata and checkpoint summary
sources.evidence: The original repository was created on 2026-01-27. Its reported revision is aaa02f3811945a91062062994c5c4a3f4c0af2b0 and safetensors total is 3389119360 BF16 elements, independently matching the bounded-header sum. Fresh October 27 metadata remains at the same revision and 3,389,119,360 BF16 aggregate, supporting retention of the prior exact census without repeating header or shard retrieval.

sources.title: Official checkpoint index
sources.evidence: The index references one safetensors shard and exactly the 2707 tensor keys present in its header. Index metadata.total_size is inconsistent with the actual header tensor-byte sum, so the count uses tensor shapes rather than index file-size arithmetic.

sources.title: Current official DeepSeek-OCR 2 repository
sources.evidence: Fresh October 27 read of the current official repository and release instructions links the same paper and checkpoint. No later active-parameter comparison or replacement specification is published there.

sources.title: DeepSeek-OCR 2 report version history
sources.evidence: Fresh October 27 check lists only the January 28 v1 submission. No revised developer paper supersedes its nominal decoder-only 500M active disclosure.

sources.title: Jina OCR v1 release and later OCR comparison
sources.evidence: Fresh exact-model count search led to the September 14, 2026 release. It describes about 570M active decoder parameters for Jina’s DeepSeek-OCR-derived model and lists DeepSeek-OCR-2 as 3B/570M in its comparison. This is a later independent developer comparison, not a revised DeepSeek specification; retain DeepSeek’s own approximate 500M convention for the exact OCR2 language decoder rather than substituting a different precision or claiming a whole-model active count.

sources.title: Independent DeepSeek-OCR-2 hardware directory entry
sources.evidence: Fresh search and October 27 read found a 1.2B active claim alongside generic links to the model card and paper. The page supplies no exact-model active-count derivation or scope explaining its difference from the original paper. It is recorded as an uncorroborated secondary lead and is not adopted.

name.note: Official model title; normalize the baseline spelling to include the published hyphen.

developer.note: Published by the official deepseek-ai account and attributed to DeepSeek-AI in the technical report.

family.note: Normalized family key for the explicitly identified DeepSeek-OCR successor.

release_date.note: The developer explicitly dates its announcement January 27; repository creation corroborates it. January 28 is the later paper date.

open_weights.note: Original model weights are publicly downloadable from the developer-owned repository under its supplied license.

license.note: Read the actual license accompanying OCR2 weights. Do not transfer the earlier DeepSeek-OCR repository MIT license.

parameters_b.note: Complete learned checkpoint count: 3389119360 parameters / 1e9. Includes text embeddings/head, all routed/shared experts, both vision components, learned query/position embeddings, projector and view separator. All 2707 tensors are BF16 learned tensors; no quantization scales or persistent buffers are counted. Header range and component arithmetic are cached in /tmp/model-audit-167/parameter-summary.json. Fresh metadata remains unchanged on October 27; the prior complete count is retained without a repeat tensor census.

active_parameters_b.note: Approximately 0.5B active language-decoder parameters, explicitly published in sections 3.3 and 4.2.2 of the exact-model report. Scope is language_decoder, whose complete parameter component is separately recorded; this excludes the vision tokenizer, causal vision encoder and projector and does not claim a full image-prefill active count. Fresh searches, current repository evidence and later comparisons found no superseding DeepSeek disclosure. Jina’s 570M comparison and an independent 1.2B claim do not replace the developer’s nominal convention.

architecture.note: Multimodal encoder/projector/decoder Transformer with a sparse MoE language decoder, not dense: 64 routed experts, 6 selected per token, 2 shared experts, and one initial dense layer. Dense SAM and Qwen2 vision components do not change the decoder classification.

context_window.note: The original language-model configuration explicitly sets 8192 positions. The separate 256–1120 visual tokens per image describe the image encoder budget, not context length; Qwen2 visual-encoder internal positional capacity is also not the decoder context.

modalities.note: Primary examples accept image input with textual OCR instructions and generate text/Markdown. PDF workflows rasterize pages; no native audio or video modality is established.

reasoning.note: The paper discusses causal visual reasoning as an architectural mechanism. It does not specify a native user-facing thinking/reasoning mode, separate reasoning output, or control; the OCR inference interface does not establish one. Clear the catalog-only false assertion rather than treating architecture wording as such a mode.

tool_call.note: No native tool/function-calling interface or training capability is documented for this OCR checkpoint. Inherited tool tokens are insufficient to confirm support or its absence; clear the catalog-only false assertion.

description.value: Open-weight OCR vision-language model that combines DeepEncoder V2 with a mixture-of-experts language decoder for text extraction and grounded document-to-Markdown conversion.
description.note: Replace the unqualified high-accuracy claim and broad scenario list with the demonstrated model structure and documented OCR/grounded conversion tasks.

patch.name: DeepSeek-OCR 2
patch.description: Open-weight OCR vision-language model that combines DeepEncoder V2 with a mixture-of-experts language decoder for text extraction and grounded document-to-Markdown conversion.
patch.notes: Complete released checkpoint: 3.38911936B learned parameters. Approximately 0.5B active parameters refers only to the language decoder, per the developer report; image encoding is separate. Decoder context is 8192; the 256–1120 tokens per image are a separate visual budget. Native thinking mode and tool calling are not established by the developer materials.

sources.label: Official repository metadata and checkpoint summary

summary: October 27 parameter re-audit retains the exact 3.38911936B complete total and exposes the developer’s nominal 0.5B active language-decoder count with explicit component scope. Fresh searches, reopened original paper/card/configuration/implementation, current metadata and later comparison leads confirm the basis and preserve the distinction from image encoding. Existing component and decoder-phase data remain; unrelated assessments are unchanged. No weight shards or repeat census requested.
